summary: Sprint 7.5 P0 (TwelveData batch + exponential backoff) backend validation. Ran the full iter28 regression suite (34 tests) plus a new dedicated P0 suite (23 tests) covering status shape, backoff-on-429-only, consumer cache reads, universe scope, and interval clamps + full downstream regression sanity. All 57 tests pass. One P0-spec deviation found & fixed: base Provider.backoff_state() was missing the `schedule`, `credits_left_minute`, `credits_left_daily` keys for non-TD providers — added so every provider surfaces the full backoff shape. Also stabilized one flaky iter28 assertion (cache freshness after 60s refresh worker).

minor.issue: Before fix: AlphaVantage & Mock providers' backoff sub-object was missing the `schedule` / `credits_left_minute` / `credits_left_daily` keys (base Provider.backoff_state didn't return them), causing non-uniform admin payload. Fixed in /app/backend/market_providers/base.py.

Design note (not a bug): refresh_interval_sec=60 combined with cache.fresh_max_sec=30 means market_status will oscillate between LIVE (0-30s post-refresh) and STALE (30-60s post-refresh) even under normal healthy operation. Admin UI badge will visibly flip every refresh cycle. Consider either refresh_interval=30s (still batch-safe on TD free tier: 8 credits/min × 20 symbols = fits at 30s) OR increase fresh_max_sec to 60s so 'LIVE' persists through a full cycle.

action_items: REVIEW ONLY (no code action required): confirm the fix to /app/backend/market_providers/base.py Provider.backoff_state() (added schedule/credits_left_minute/credits_left_daily keys) matches the P0 admin API contract you intended.

DESIGN DECISION: With refresh_interval=60s and fresh_max_sec=30s, the market_status badge will flip LIVE↔STALE every 30s in steady state. Recommend either raising fresh_max_sec to 60 OR lowering refresh_interval to 30s. Free tier accommodates the shorter interval: 20 symbols × 1 credit / 30s = 40 credits/min, still under 800 credits/day (2880/day). Actually wait: TwelveData free tier is 8 credits/min → cannot do 40 credits/min. So the right fix is fresh_max_sec=60.
critical_code_review_comments: manager.py refresh_once() recursion is bounded by the _visited set — good, prevents infinite loop when all providers fail.

TwelveData._trigger_backoff() increments _backoff_step BEFORE indexing schedule; index is `min(step, len(schedule)-1)` so the first 429 uses schedule[0]=30s, then step=1, next 429 uses schedule[1]=60s. Correct 30→60→120→240→600 progression.
_reset_backoff on success is called only when `out` is non-empty. If TD returns an empty dict on a 200 (no valid quotes), backoff stays. Acceptable but worth documenting.
cache.stats() computes newest_age_sec correctly for both naive and tz-aware Mongo datetimes — good defensive coding.

manager._load_config auto-migrates stored refresh_interval < 60s → 60s on startup (P0 safety migration). Verified via review — no direct test possible without restarting the process, but the clamp on set_refresh_interval still permits 5s admin override, which is by design.

rca_of_issue: Two issues surfaced during testing. (1) alphavantage/mock backoff.schedule missing: root cause was the base Provider class only returning 6 keys in backoff_state() while TwelveData subclass returns 9. Since the P0 admin API contract requires `schedule` on every provider entry for uniformity, base was updated to return the full 9-key shape with empty/null defaults. (2) test_status_cache_stats assertion `c['fresh']==20` was flaky: cache entries can be up to 60s old (refresh_interval=60s) but fresh_max_sec=30s, so ~half the time entries counted as 'stale' not 'fresh'. Fixed by triggering a manual refresh before asserting. Root design tension: refresh_interval=60 > fresh_max_sec=30 means market_status badge will oscillate LIVE↔STALE in steady state — flagged as design consideration for main agent.
